subject.title: [Architecture] Isolate terminal PTY execution drivers into dedicated package

question: Should OpenClaw create and support a reusable terminal PTY execution boundary now, or keep PTY lifecycle ownership local to the TUI until a concrete headless consumer exists?
rationale: The request is an architectural investment rather than a demonstrated regression, and choosing a package-level API without an identified consumer would set a potentially long-lived internal contract.

options.title: Wait for a concrete consumer
options.body: Keep the current local boundary and reopen or refine this work when a headless task has a defined PTY lifecycle contract.

options.title: Sponsor a reusable core boundary
options.body: Assign an owner to define the minimal cross-runtime PTY API, ownership rules, and focused migration plan before implementation.

recommendation.title: Wait for a concrete consumer
recommendation.body: Keep the current local boundary and reopen or refine this work when a headless task has a defined PTY lifecycle contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter can clarify the intended headless use case; a code-history owner should be added after maintainer source review.
